touches.text: Trouble Ticket: an error that needs a non-automated fixer (CC or Akien).
A diagnostic report, EXACTLY like the Trouble Tickets in the Number Five Crossbar Telephone Switch. It MUST include EVERYTHING needed to diagnose, isolate, and repair the trouble.
A second observation of an open trouble NEVER issues a new ticket; it increments a counter on the open one.
The test before raising one: can only CC or Akien fix this? If not, it is a log line, not a trouble. One problem, one trouble.
They show on the operator's to-do list (7.3.6).
Trouble tickets (3.4.3) live here. Any device has a direct line to raise one, not over the bus (2.3.7.1.3).
Runs a proof as its own process and writes a validation record (claim, caller, date, method, verdict, evidence, falsifier, horizon).

Reds don't get lost. Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds and every orphaned file it sees, unless one is already open for it. A red seen in passing gets the same treatment. Every red and every orphaned file is fixed; one unrelated to the work in hand is ticketed, and once it is, that crossing can go ahead.
Test tiers: commit, hourly, daily and weekly. Each tier runs only what it must, so a commit needs only its own proofs and the long runs wait for the long tiers; nothing runs just in case.

A red seen in passing gets the same treatment. Every red and every orphaned file is fixed; one unrelated to the work in hand is ticketed, and once it is, that crossing can go ahead.
conflicts.ticket_says: When a door refuses to write a red's ticket, run_proof catches RedTicketRefused, raises an unticketed trouble, and re-raises the exception so the run exits without writing a ticket for that red. The red stays new for the next run to retry.
conflicts.why: The outline states: "Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds and every orphaned file it sees, unless one is already open for it." When the ticket's work is built, some runs (those where a door refuses) will NOT write a ticket for a new red they found. The outline's exception clause ("unless one is already open") does not cover door refusal—a gate refusing is a new situation the outline did not anticipate. This violates the stated requirement that each run writes a ticket.
